title: Anthropic Appeals Pentagon AI Blacklist
summary: Gotrade News - Anthropic asked the D.C. Circuit appeals court on October 13 to rehear its challenge to the Pentagon's supply-chain risk label, according
body_markdown:
## Why the Pentagon Labeled Anthropic a Supply-Chain Risk


The designation was made under the Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act of 2018 after Anthropic refused to drop contract limits on using Claude for lethal autonomous warfare and mass surveillance of Americans, according to[Unite.AI](https://www.unite.ai/anthropic-asks-d-c-circuit-to-rehear-pentagon-supply-chain-risk-case/) .


The formal determination was issued on March 3, 2026, following a February standoff between CEO Dario Amodei and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.


As reported by the[Associated Press](https://www.clickondetroit.com/business/2026/09/25/federal-court-says-us-government-can-label-anthropic-a-supply-chain-risk/) , the September ruling allows the Pentagon to remove Claude from its systems, bar Anthropic products from Defense Department work and prohibit contractors from using them in that work, though the products are not barred from the federal government as a whole.


Judge Gregory Katsas wrote that the definition turns "on what Anthropic does, not why Anthropic does it," while Judge Karen LeCraft Henderson dissented.


> "Another federal court has already held the government's parallel designation unlawful." Anthropic statement, September 25, 2026, via the Associated Press


Pentagon chief spokesman Sean Parnell said the ruling "completely validates the Department's position," per the AP. In a separate case, a federal judge in California found this summer that the Pentagon acted illegally by punishing Anthropic for criticizing its views on AI use.


## Amazon (AMZN): Investor and Cloud Partner in the Dispute


[Amazon (AMZN)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/amzn/) is an Anthropic investor, and Anthropic first worked with classified information through a supply deal via Amazon's cloud, according to[Reuters](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/exclusive-anthropic-investors-push-escalate-165705249.html) . Reuters reported in March that Amazon CEO Andy Jassy had discussed the Pentagon dispute with Amodei, and that investors were focused on avoiding the designation because it could seriously hurt Anthropic's sales to business customers.


## Alphabet (GOOGL): Pentagon Contracts as Anthropic Sits Out


Google, owned by[Alphabet (GOOGL)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/googl/) , and OpenAI have won Pentagon contracts through streamlined procurement while Anthropic is excluded from those opportunities, according to[The Tech Buzz](https://www.techbuzz.ai/articles/anthropic-appeals-pentagon-ai-blacklist-in-federal-court) . The outlet cited projections that defense AI spending will reach $15 billion a year by 2027.


The Tech Buzz also reported that Anthropic is courting investors ahead of a potential[IPO](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/what-is-an-ipo/) , and that Pentagon revenue could affect its valuation.


Legal observers quoted in that report expect the case to test whether the Pentagon followed proper procedures and whether its security justifications hold up.
